newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica finance dept unaware big municipal default.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica finance dept unaware big municipal default.

text.p: South Africa's finance department said on Tuesday it was unaware of any major debt default by municipalities.

"I have no knowledge of that whatsoever, of local authorities failing or anything of the sort. It is news to me and I would imagine it is just a rumour," Coen Kruger, chief director of asset and liability management, told Reuters.
Rumours of a big municipal debt default hit the debt market on Tuesday with rates on the benchmark R150 long bond kicking up to 15.15 percent from 15.05 on Monday.
Dealers said concerns about municipal debt may have been raised by comments from Provincial Affairs Minister Mohammed Valli Moosa earlier today in Cape Town.
He said that about a third of municipalities were viable and able to exercise sound fiscal control, about a third were "stressed" and about a third were "not viable".

He also said the Local Authorities Loans Fund experienced its first default in its 18-year history at the end of June 1995. By the end of 1996, 48 municipalities were in default, though the nine million rand total owed represented barely one percent of the 880 million rand loan book.
Valli Moosa said the total owed to local authorities had risen from five billion rand in June 1995 to six billion rand in October last year.

He said that though the number of municipal accounts paid regularly had not risen above 68 percent in the past year, he believed the South African local government financing crisis had "bottomed out" and that the situation was improving.

"We now have a macro picture of the state of local government financing. It tells us that the situation is far from satisfactory, but we don't think the situation is deteriorating at this time," he said.
Dealers said the bond market also appeared to have weakened following funding activities by the Reserve Bank, although industry sources said this funding was routine at the fiscal year end.
